A: Wow, can you believe it? Venezuela just won the World Baseball Classic!

B: I know, right? It’s absolutely wild! They knocked off the U.S. and Japan along the way. I mean, that’s a serious power move in the baseball world.

A: Seriously! For the first time ever, they can call themselves the best in the world. I think it’s about time we recognize them as a baseball powerhouse, don’t you?

B: Totally! I mean, it’s like they flipped the script from last tournament. Remember how their bullpen collapsed? This time, they delivered 6 1/3 scoreless innings against Japan and then followed that up with 7 2/3 shutout frames against Italy. That’s just insane!

A: Right? And it’s not just about winning; it’s how they did it. Their bullpen was like a brick wall! I can’t help but think how different the narrative would’ve been if Trea Turner’s grand slam hadn’t ended their run last time.

B: Oh, for sure! That’s gotta feel good for them, getting that redemption. And can we just talk about the excitement surrounding the WBC? It’s like a whole different vibe compared to the regular MLB season. 

A: Exactly! It’s high-stakes, emotionally charged, and honestly, it feels like the playoffs in October. I mean, who doesn’t love that rush?

B: Right? It’s like every game matters so much more. I was glued to my screen, yelling at my TV like it was game seven of the World Series. 

A: Same! And it’s cool how this tournament has really put international baseball on the map. It’s like the Olympics or the World Cup, but for baseball. You can really feel the passion from fans around the world.

B: Definitely! And I loved hearing the comments from Mexico’s manager, Benji Gil, after their semifinal loss in 2023. He said, “Japan moved on, but the world of baseball won today.” That sentiment still rings true!

A: Oh, absolutely! It’s like the spirit of the sport is thriving globally. And speaking of winners, Venezuela’s bullpen is clearly a standout. But who else do you think came out ahead in this tournament?

B: Well, I think the whole concept of the WBC being “appointment viewing” is a huge win for baseball. People are tuning in and getting excited, which is what the sport needs, you know? 

A: For sure! It’s all about creating those moments that get fans hyped. So, any predictions for the next WBC? 

B: Hmm, that’s a tough one. But if Venezuela keeps building on this success, they could become a formidable force in future tournaments. 

A: Right? I can see them being a real contender. But then again, you can’t count out the U.S. or Japan; they’ll be back with a vengeance. 

B: Oh, you know it! It’s gonna be a battle for sure. I can’t wait for the next one! 

A: Same here! Here’s to more thrilling baseball moments ahead!

SOURCE TITLE: The Winners and Losers of the 2026 World Baseball Classic
SOURCE CONTENT: For the second consecutive World Baseball Classic, the United States walked off the field one run short, losing 3-2 in the final to a proud baseballing nation. Venezuela claimed its first WBC title, knocking off both Japan and the U.S. along the way and announcing itself as the sport’s newest powerhouse.
And yet, much like 2023, the most lasting takeaway won’t be that the Americans lost, but that this tournament has become appointment viewing. For two weeks every three years, the sport sheds its leisurely pace and turns into a high-stakes and emotionally charged spectacle rivaled only by October in intensity—at least in Major League Baseball. The World Baseball Classic gives international baseball a spot on the sports map next to the Olympics and the World Cup and reveals a version of the sport that feels louder and more urgent than the one we watch most of the year.
Mexico manager Benji Gil said in 2023 that “Japan moved on, but the world of baseball won today,” after his team’s crushing semifinal loss on a walk-off. Three years later, that sentiment feels even more true. Baseball is the unquestioned winner once again. But, of course, there are some other specific figures who can hold their heads up high.
Here are the winners and losers of the 2026 World Baseball Classic.
Winner: Venezuela, Obviously (and Its Bullpen Especially)
In a continent dominated by soccer, Venezuela has long stood alone as South America’s true baseball nation. Now, for the first time, it can call itself the best in the world.
The primary difference was on the mound. Three years after its bullpen collapsed in the quarterfinal—when Trea Turner’s grand slam ended the team’s run—Venezuela flipped the script entirely. This time, its relievers were nearly untouchable at the business end of the tournament.
